briefing:
On September 8, 2026, the composite daily Airfare Price Index (APIx) registered a modest uptick of 0.43% over baseline levels to stand at 100.43, indicating general baseline stability across domestic trunk routes accompanied by localized near-term upward pressure. Market movements were top-line positive but regionally divergent across the intelligence pipeline's three primary flight corridors. The inflationary impetus was led by the Calcutta–Bombay route, which recorded the highest route-level APIx of 102.02 (a 2.02% increase over baseline), complemented by a mild firming on Delhi–Bombay at 100.45 (+0.45%). Conversely, the North–South Delhi–Bengaluru corridor served as a deflationary counterweight, contracting by 1.19% to a route-level APIx of 98.81.

A granular examination of advance booking windows reveals that the headline increase was overwhelmingly driven by acute price surges in immediate departure dates (T+1 window). In the Calcutta–Bombay corridor, the T+1 median fare spiked by 33.66% from ₹9,584 to ₹12,810, while Delhi–Bombay T+1 median fares escalated by 14.47% from ₹6,530 to ₹7,475. In contrast, intermediate advance purchase windows demonstrated disinflationary trends across all routes; T+15 and T+30 price relativities registered consistent declines, with Delhi–Bengaluru T+15 falling 7.56% below baseline (price relativity of 92.44) and Calcutta–Bombay T+15 dropping 4.20% (price relativity of 95.80). Extended purchase horizons (T+45) reflected moderate carrier yield strengthening across all corridors, ranging from a 0.29% rise on Delhi–Bengaluru to a 6.86% increase on Calcutta–Bombay.

Underlying scraped micro-data highlights notable price dispersion and structural market adjustments across carrier strategies and regional airport infrastructure. In the Delhi NCR and Mumbai metropolitan clusters, the operationalization of regional secondary hubs provided visible price relief; for instance, Akasa Air departing from Jewar (DXN) offered T+7 fares at ₹5,382 compared to the ₹6,530 standard rate for mainline Delhi–Bombay non-stop flights. Severe upper-tail fare escalation was observed in last-minute Calcutta–Bombay flights, where non-stop prime-time services reached up to ₹16,200 for IndiGo and ₹13,848 for Air India, dragging the median upward despite single-stop options existing around ₹9,041. Additionally, targeted carrier discounting was evident in the T+7 Delhi–Bengaluru segment, where Air India deal fares dipped to ₹7,787, undercutting the route median of ₹9,221.

Looking ahead, domestic airfares exhibit a clear structural dichotomy: persistent carrier pricing power and high demand inelasticity on near-term departures contrast with stable, competitive pricing in the 15-to-30 day advance booking windows. From a macro-monetary policy perspective, while last-minute airfare surges introduce transient volatility into the transport component of the Consumer Price Index, anchored forward curves suggest minimal pass-through into medium-term inflation expectations. Policy makers at the Reserve Bank of India and MoSPI should continue to monitor capacity constraints on high-utilization corridors like Calcutta–Bombay, while anticipating that general passenger transport inflation will remain range-bound in the upcoming policy cycle.
